entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Veturius Geminus Cicurinus was a prominent Roman politician of the 5th century BC, who served as Consul of Rome in 499 BC alongside Titus Aebutius Helva. Born into the patrician class and the Veturia gens, Cicurinus was a member of Rome's elite.

As a key figure in the early 5th century BC, Cicurinus played a significant role in shaping Rome's political landscape. His service as Consul was marked by the passage of several important laws, including the Lex Aebutia, which had a lasting impact on Roman governance.

Cicurinus's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he influenced the development of Roman law and politics. His contributions to the Lex Aebutia have been studied by historians for centuries, providing valuable insights into the workings of ancient Roman government.


Gaius Veturius Geminus Cicurinus was a key player in Rome's early 5th century BC politics, whose service as Consul left a lasting impact on Roman governance and law.
